messages:
toby: hey folks, day 1 question - i imported the kubeconfig from Okta and ran `kubectl get pods -n pricing` and got a Forbidden error. not sure who owns the namespace or the quick fix. any tips?

toby: exact error: `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "toby@redwood.com" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "pricing"`

devops: welcome! quick checks: 1) `kubectl config current-context` 2) `kubectl config view --minify` 3) `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=pricing` - paste outputs (no tokens).

toby: `kubectl config current-context` -> `prod-toby`
toby: `kubectl config view --minify` -> shows user `toby@redwood.com`, cluster `prod`
toby: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=pricing` -> `no`

lisa: hey toby, pricing is owned by eng-pricing. we gate via SSO group `eng-pricing-devs`. if your Okta->k8s group mapping hasn't synced you won't see perms yet. what's your SSO id and github handle?

toby: SSO: toby@redwood.com, github: tobydev

lisa: cool. i can add a namespace-scoped RoleBinding with `view` for a few hours so you can finish onboarding. i avoid ClusterRoleBindings for new hires. creating now.

lisa: command i ran (dry-run -> apply):
```
kubectl create rolebinding onb-toby-pricing -n pricing --clusterrole=view --user=toby@redwood.com --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

lisa: done. retry `kubectl get pods -n pricing`

toby: retried -> pods list now shows up, thanks!! :tada:

toby: couple follow-ups: 1) how long do these temp bindings live? 2) any safe workflow to avoid hitting prod accidentally (i merged kubeconfigs earlier)?

devops: 1) i set this one to expire after 8h; we log them for audit. 2) best practices: keep prod kubeconfig separate, or use `kubectx`/`kubens` for context/namespace switching. `kubectl config use-context <name>` is the native way. also consider a prompt segment showing `kubectl config current-context`.

lisa: for persistent access open the infra access form (it assigns the SSO group): https://internal.redwood/infra/access - that hooks into Okta and our group-sync. temporary RoleBindings are just for onboarding.

infra-bot: Reminder: onboarding doc "kube-access" updated with group mapping troubleshooting steps -> https://internal.redwood/docs/onboard/kube-access. Do not request ClusterRoleBinding unless you need cluster-wide perms.

toby: thanks everyone! adding notes to my checklist. also installing kubectx/kubens now.
